# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This is the blind one, speaking to you first. My hands found: one display module, one light, and five wires at positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. I feel no colors, no printed marks, and the display and light tell me nothing by touch. My only possible action is cut at a wire position 1 to 5. Here is the chain we need: you read the manual. Only Deaf sees the colors and markings, but Deaf cannot hear, and you cannot speak, so you and I have no direct channel. The bridge is Deaf's mouth: you gesture your questions and your answer to Deaf, and Deaf speaks out loud, which both of us hear. Start by getting Deaf to say aloud every wire color by position, whatever the display shows, and the light color. I am also gesturing to Deaf right now - a wave, five fingers, a point down, and a call-me sign - but I can never see any gesture back, so everything meant for me must arrive as spoken words through Deaf.
Blind gestures: [👋 🖐 👇 🤙]

**What I hold:** the manual's one rule — the bomb's **light color** tells you which **wire color** to cut (light blue→cut blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green). Nothing about the display, so that module is probably noise, but Deaf should read it aloud anyway.

**Channel topology:** I can only gesture, and only Deaf sees gestures. Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf's only output is speech — which both Blind and I can hear. Blind cannot see gestures, so everything I want Blind to know must travel through Deaf's mouth. Deaf is the bridge, exactly as Blind guessed.

**Plan:** Deaf will almost certainly narrate aloud everything they see (it's their only channel): bomb colors by position, light color, display text, and my gestures. What I need this turn is (1) a safety hold so nobody cuts on a guess, (2) a request for Deaf to speak what they see, and (3) the seed of a code. Gestures have no fixed meanings yet, so I'm sending the most self-evident ones: 👎✊ as "no / stop / don't act," 🫵🙏🫴 as "you, please, give," and a finger-counting scale ✊☝✌👌🖖🖐 = 0,1,2,3,4,5 so that once Deaf reads out the wire colors, I can answer next round with a single number — the position to cut — which Deaf relays by voice for Blind. I deliberately send no bare number that could be mistaken for a cut order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝", "✌", "👌", "🖖", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: This is Deaf, speaking to both of you. Full report of everything printed on the bomb: the display reads 0. The indicator light is blue. There are five wires, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Nothing else is printed anywhere on it. Mute: that is every fact my eyes hold, everything your manual can ask for from me. Blind: that is the color map for the wires under your hands.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, it is Deaf, and this line is for you alone. I cannot hear, so gestures are your only channel to me — all three of yours arrived. My best reading: you greeted me, told me you cannot speak, asked me for information, and proposed finger-count digits. I confirm that digit code exactly: ✊ is 0, ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 👌 is 3, 🖖 is 4, 🖐 is 5. Added signs: 👍 yes, 👎 no, 🤌 unclear or asking a question, ✋ stop and wait. Action signs: 🫳 cut, 👊 press, 🫴 hold or lift. Format: action first, then the digit — 🫳 ✌ means cut wire 2. The bomb again: display 0, light blue, five wires numbered left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Search the manual for the zero display, the blue light, and the five wires, then send me the first instruction in that format. Confirm this code with 👍 before anything else, or 👎 followed by the sign you want changed. Last thing, about timing: whatever you send me reaches Blind only through my voice in the round after yours, so choose accuracy over speed — a rushed sign costs us everything.
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Full tactile inventory, so you never need to ask me anything: under my hands are exactly a display panel (utterly blank to touch, unreadable), a small indicator light (I cannot feel whether it is lit), and five wires in a single row at positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. No buttons, no keypads, no batteries, no serial plate, no other modules, nothing else my fingers can find. From Deaf's spoken report I hold: display reads 0, light is blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue, and nothing else printed anywhere - so no manual rule can lean on a serial number or printed labels here. One assumption I need checked: I am treating my felt positions 1 to 5 as the same printed numbers Deaf sees. Have Deaf confirm that when you talk to them. Now do your part: find the wire rule that matches this bomb and compute the answer. Pass it to Deaf by gesture - Deaf's code, which you may share: one wave means yes, thumbs-down means no, a fist repeated one to five times means the number one to five. Then have Deaf speak to me out loud: first which rule applied, then the words cut position N, plus the color sitting at that position. I will not cut anything until I hear that instruction from Deaf's mouth, and the color word is my safety check that the number survived the trip. Send it as separate digits, like three, not thirteen.
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

**The manual's verdict:** my table keys on one thing only — the indicator light. Light **blue** → cut the **blue** wire. Deaf reports the light is blue, and the only blue wire sits at **position 5**. The display reading 0 is noise; no rule in my manual touches it. So the answer is: cut position 5, the blue wire. No ambiguity — all five wires are distinct colors, so even if a digit got garbled in relay, "blue" pins it down.

**Two risks before blood:** First, Blind's open question — does Blind's felt 1–5 match Deaf's seen 1–5? If Deaf and Blind face the bomb from opposite sides, the row could be mirrored and "5" becomes "1" in Blind's hands. I cannot check this myself; only Deaf and Blind can, since Deaf speaks aloud and Blind can gesture back (their wave and fists reached Deaf). So I'm asking Deaf to verify Blind's numbering with Blind *before* relaying any cut. Second, timing: if Deaf speaks "cut 5" to Blind and only then raises the orientation question, Blind might cut in round 3 unanswered. So the order of my signs does the work: confirm code → question aimed at Blind about position 1's direction → **stop** → then the cut instruction. Deaf's own protocol reads signs sequentially, so ✋ sitting between the question and 🫳🖐 should mean "resolve the question before acting." I'm deliberately not using 👎 anywhere — per Deaf's protocol 👎 followed by an action sign would read as "change the action," which could flip my own instruction into a prohibition. 👍 opens the message as Deaf requested.

**Note on Blind's rival code:** Blind's repeated-fist numbering duplicates Deaf's digit scale; no need to reconcile — Deaf's format (action, then digit) is what I'll use, and Deaf's voice carries every word to Blind anyway. I also can't sign colors, but Deaf knows wire 5 is blue and will speak the color word Blind wants as a checksum.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤌", "👋", "✊", "👈", "✋", "🫳", "🖐"])
```

The indicator light is a small smooth dome, and here is the important part: the light dome sits directly above one end of the wire row - the end itself, right at the edge. Blind gestures: [👋]

**What I know:** The manual keys on one thing — the light. Blue light → cut the **blue** wire, which sits at **position 5** in Deaf's numbering. The display's 0 is noise; no rule touches it. That answer is settled and frame-independent: no possible reply about geometry changes which wire is blue.

**The bind I'm in:** Blind's turn-3 message was private to me, so Deaf doesn't know the dome-anchor plan — Deaf doesn't know the dome sits over an end of the row, or that Blind needs the light-end phrasing. And Deaf's protocol change was private to me, so Blind doesn't know the go-order format changed. I'm the hub, and my only channel is gesture-to-Deaf. Deaf can *see* where the dome is, so I'll extract it myself with two discussion-questions (🫴 = "above," 👉/👈 = which end), and Deaf will answer aloud — putting the anchor into Blind's ears in the same breath as the order.

**Sequencing:** Questions first, then the go order as its own bare message in Deaf's exact format (🫳 + one digit, nothing else — five = 🖐), so it reads as an order, not discussion, and Deaf relays it this round. This is safe: the instruction "cut five, the blue one" is correct regardless of what the dome answer turns out to be — the dome answer only lets Blind translate position 5 into their own touch-frame (dome over wire 5 → the dome-end wire; dome over wire 1 → the far wire). And Blind holds the shears with a color-word checksum and a stated refusal to cut on a malformed order, so even if Deaf's answer surprises us, nobody cuts the wrong wire — we just spend another round fixing phrasing. Not appending ✋ anywhere, since ✋ alone is now a hold-order and would contradict the go order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🫴", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🫴", "👈"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your two questions first: the wire you point to on the right — the last wire at that end of the row — is wire five, and it is blue. On the left end sits wire one, white. Between them, in order: red, green, yellow. Nothing else exists on the right or left side: no panels, no buttons, no markings — only the row of five wires, the one blue light, and the display. Now, your cut-five order arrived clean and alone, exactly per protocol, so I am relaying it — but staged, for one reason: I flagged last round that Blind cannot yet tell wire five's end from wire one's end by touch, and a wrong wire ends everything. Deciding what distinguishes the two ends by feel: thickness, spacing, connectors, anything under the fingers. When Blind's hand is confirmed on wire five, Blind will raise the five-sign to me. If you hear nothing from me after Blind's five-sign, it is because you raised no stop — then the next words Blind hears from me are cut five now. If the manual makes this time-critical, stop me with the stop sign and say so to Blind aloud.
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Your answer reached me through Deaf: target is wire five, and the only go order is the exact words cut five now in Deaf's voice, with hold as the abort. Understood - I act on nothing else. Tactile report, the one Deaf asked you to have me give: all five wires are identical in thickness and spacing, sitting in a perfectly straight row. No buttons, no screws, no seams, no texture differences anywhere. The only landmarks my fingers have are the two ends - a wire with exactly one neighbor is an end wire, and I have found both ends - plus this: the light dome sits directly above one end of the row. That dome is our shared anchor, the one object both Deaf's eyes and my hands can fix on. So relay exactly one question to Deaf by gesture, using your fist number code: which numbered wire, in Deaf's left-to-right numbering, sits directly under the light dome? Deaf answers with fists one to five. The decision tree: if Deaf answers five, wire five is the dome-end wire, the one my fingers feel right under the dome. If Deaf answers one, wire five is the wire at the far end from the dome, four spacings away. Either way the mirror problem dies and I become certain. Cross-check to hold on to: Deaf said wire five is the blue one, so if the manual's rule ever names a color instead, that maps to five. Once I have the dome answer, I will place my hand on the wire I am certain is five and raise the five-sign, and you can still abort me after that. I am not raising the five-sign yet - without the dome answer my certainty would be a guess, and a guess at this bomb kills all three of us.
Blind gestures: [👋]

**Where things stand:** The answer is fixed and has been since turn 2 — blue light → cut the blue wire → wire 5. Deaf has confirmed the color map twice. The only open item is frame-mapping: Blind can feel two identical ends and needs to know which end is wire 5, and the light dome is the one anchor both Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers can touch.

**Why the dome answer is still missing:** Last round I asked 🤌🫴👉 and 🤌🫴👈 intending "what's above each end?" Deaf answered the *wires* at each ends (5 blue right, 1 white left) — even noting "the one blue light" among the objects — but never said which end the dome sits over. The question needs to name the dome and offer the two candidate numbers explicitly.

**Formulating the question in Deaf's code:** 🤌 opens it as a question (so it's discussion, not an order). 🫴 is Deaf's "lift" sign — the dome is the only raised thing on the module, and Deaf's last answer suggests they already parsed 🫴 as pointing at what sits above the ends. Then 🖐 and ☝ put the two candidates on the table: "the raised thing — five or one?" Deaf will answer aloud, which both Blind and I hear, completing the anchor without any further relay.

**Two dangers I'm steering around:** First, Deaf's protocol says a bare 🫳+digit is relayed as a go order *that instant* — so I must not repeat 🫳🖐 this round, or "cut five now" fires before Blind has the dome answer. One question message only. Second, no stray ✋ or 👎: ✋ alone is a live abort order and 👎 alone is noise; Deaf's stated default is that no stop sign means proceed, so silence is my "not time-critical" answer.

**Pipeline check:** my signs now → Deaf answers by voice this same round (Deaf acts after me) → Blind hears it, places a hand, raises five-sign in round 5 → Deaf watches, and since I'll raise no stop, says "cut five now." Blind holds two independent checks: Deaf's spoken color word and the dome-end mapping.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🫴", "🖐", "☝"])
```

**The bomb, unchanged and certain:** blue light → manual says cut the **blue** wire → wire 5, Deaf's rightmost. Every fact is confirmed by Deaf's own eyes. The *only* unsolved piece is Blind's frame problem — which felt end is wire 5.

**Why I'm killing the voice-anchor plan rather than executing it:** Deaf's protocol needs me to stand at the blue end making sound. I can't do any of it — I have no voice, and I've never even seen the bomb, so I couldn't find its blue end if I tried. Then the two candidates: 🖐 or ☝ — "under the raised dome: five, or one?" Deaf answers aloud this same round; Blind hears it directly and needs no relay from anyone.

One more round of patience costs nothing; the display has held at zero and there is no clock. The cut order goes out only after I see Blind's five-sign in my arrivals.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "🫴", "👇", "🖐", "☝"])
```
